title: Managing product delivery: activities, inputs, outputs and RACI
blurb: Place a team manager's action in the right managing product delivery activity, judge it against the recommended actions, and answer RACI questions on executing and completing work packages.
question: A project board member asks a supplier's team manager directly to add a feature during the work. The team manager adds it straight away. Which activity is affected, is this appropriate, and who should the team manager take instructions from?

teach.h: The team manager's side of the work package
teach.body: Managing product delivery controls the link between the project manager and the team manager. It agrees what is needed for acceptance, execution, reporting and delivery of specialist products. It is the team manager's view of a work package, as controlling a stage is the PM's. The project board is not involved, and a supplier does not need to use PRINCE2: a Scrum team can deliver a PRINCE2 work package.

teach.h: Why the RACI looks like this
teach.body: The work package is the PM's delegated authority, so the PM is accountable while the team manager does the work. Project assurance is consulted because it checks, on the board's behalf, that products are being built properly. The board is not involved in this process, which is why the business layer and executive have no part in executing the work. Project support is informed of completion so it can keep the registers up to date.

children.edge: New issue, risk or lesson, or WP tolerance forecast to break
children.label: Notify the project manager

teach.caption: Every new issue, risk or lesson goes to the PM, never straight to the board. The PM decides in controlling a stage whether to correct or escalate.

teach.body: For the discovery and alpha stage of Permits Online, project manager Hannah Okoro co-creates a work package with Kestrel Lane's delivery manager Tom Achebe: a tested prototype, fortnightly checkpoint reports after each sprint review, and scope, cost and time tolerances. Tom checks the work is achievable and accepts it. His Scrum team builds in sprints; after an accessibility test he updates the quality register, and he tells Hannah about a new risk with a screen reader. When the work is done he notifies Hannah, and project support is informed.

teach.text: Traps: (1) The team manager takes instructions from the PM, not directly from board members. (2) Work package tolerances cover scope, cost and time; benefits and quality tolerances are not agreed in a WPD. (3) Checkpoint reports go from the team manager to the PM; highlight reports go from the PM to the board. (4) Senior supplier, senior user and business layer are NOT informed of work package completion; project support is.

items: MP = the team manager's view: accept, execute, evaluate, notify completion.
Accept: agree what, reporting, constraints, procedures and whether it is achievable; team plan if needed.
Execute: build to the WPD, notify the PM of new issues, risks and lessons, update the quality register, report status.
Execute RACI: PM accountable, team manager responsible, project assurance consulted; business layer and executive not involved.

summary: You can now place a team manager's action in the right managing product delivery activity and judge whether it follows the recommended actions. You can also answer RACI questions on executing a work package and notifying its completion.

A.q: Calderbrook Borough Council is building Permits Online with Kestrel Lane Digital. Before the alpha work starts, Kestrel Lane's delivery manager Tom Achebe and project manager Hannah Okoro agree what will be delivered, how often Tom will report, the accessibility constraints, and whether the work can be done in ten weeks. Tom then confirms he will deliver it. Which 'managing product delivery' activity is Tom carrying out?
options: Authorize a work package
Accept a work package
Execute a work package
Evaluate a work package
A.why: In accept a work package, the PM and team manager agree what is to be delivered, the reporting requirements, constraints and procedures, and whether the work is achievable; the team manager then agrees to deliver it (17.4.1).

whyNot.0: Authorize a work package is the PM's activity in controlling a stage; Tom's agreement is the team manager's side, in MP.
whyNot.2: Execute a work package is the building of the products, which starts after the work package has been accepted.
whyNot.3: Evaluate a work package reports results back to the PM during or after the work, not before it starts.

A.q: During the alpha stage of Permits Online, Tom Achebe's Scrum team builds and tests prototype screens under the work package agreed with Hannah Okoro. Which role should be accountable for the 'execute a work package' activity?
options: Team manager
Project assurance
Project manager
Executive
A.why: In the RACI for execute a work package, the project manager is accountable; the team manager does the work (17.6, table 17.2).

whyNot.0: Tom is responsible for the work, including checkpoint reports, but accountability for the work package sits with the PM.
whyNot.1: Project assurance is consulted in execute a work package.
whyNot.3: The executive is not involved in execute a work package; the board does not take part in MP.

A.q: Tom Achebe's team completes an accessibility test of the alpha prototype with residents who use screen readers. Tom updates the quality register and tells Hannah Okoro the test is done. Three sprints of the work package are still to run. Which 'managing product delivery' activity is Tom carrying out?
options: Notify work package completion
Accept a work package
Evaluate a work package
Execute a work package
A.why: Execute a work package includes notifying the PM of completed quality activities and updating the quality register, alongside building the products (17.4.2).

whyNot.0: The work package is not finished; notifying completion happens when all its products are done.
whyNot.1: The work package was accepted before the sprints began.
whyNot.2: Evaluate a work package reports overall results so progress is visible; recording a completed quality activity is part of execution.

B.q: At the end of the alpha, Tom Achebe notifies Hannah Okoro that the work package is complete. Siobhan Kerr, Kestrel Lane's delivery director and the project's senior supplier, asks to be informed through the RACI each time a work package is completed. Which statement about the RACI for 'notify work package completion' is correct?
options: The senior supplier is informed; project support is not
The senior user and project support are both informed
The business layer is informed through the executive
Project support is informed; the senior supplier is not
B.why: In notify work package completion, project support is informed; the business layer, senior user and senior supplier are not (17.6, table 17.2).

whyNot.0: This reverses the RACI: project support is informed and the senior supplier is not.
whyNot.1: Project support is informed, but the senior user is not.
whyNot.2: The business layer is not informed of work package completion.

B.q: Priya Lal provides project assurance on Permits Online. She wants to give her view before Tom Achebe's team changes how it tests accessibility during the alpha work package. Under the RACI for 'execute a work package', what is project assurance's part?
options: Consulted
Accountable
Informed
Not involved
B.why: Project assurance is consulted in execute a work package (17.6, table 17.2).

whyNot.1: The project manager is accountable for execute a work package.
whyNot.2: Project assurance is consulted, which means giving input, not just being told afterwards.
whyNot.3: It is the business layer and executive that are not involved in this activity.

B.q: Tom Achebe wants to set out how his six-person team will schedule the alpha work across five sprints, in more detail than the stage plan gives. Which product should he create, and in which activity?
options: A stage plan, in 'accept a work package'
A team plan, in 'authorize a work package'
A team plan, in 'accept a work package'
A WPD, in 'execute a work package'
B.why: A team plan is optional and is produced by the team manager when accepting a work package (17.4.1).

whyNot.0: Stage plans are produced by the PM in managing a stage boundary, not by the team manager.
whyNot.1: Authorize a work package is the PM's controlling a stage activity; the team plan belongs to the team manager in MP.
whyNot.3: The WPD is co-created when the work package is authorized; it is not created during execution.

C.q: Cllr Margaret Doyle, a member of the Permits Online project board, emails Tom Achebe directly asking him to add a large-print paper application to the alpha prototype. Tom adds it to the next sprint straight away and mentions it in his next checkpoint report. Is this an appropriate application of the 'execute a work package' activity, and why?
options: Yes, because Scrum teams reprioritize their work at each sprint
Yes, because board members give direction to the whole project
No, because the team manager takes required actions from the PM
No, because the request should first appear in a checkpoint report
C.why: In execute a work package the team manager notifies the PM of new issues and takes any action required by the PM, not by board members directly. The board is not involved in MP (17.4.2, 17.3).

whyNot.0: A Scrum team can reprioritize within its work package, but a new requirement from a board member is a change that must go through the PM.
whyNot.1: The board directs the project through the PM, not by instructing team managers.
whyNot.3: Reporting the request later does not fix the problem: Tom should have referred it to Hannah before acting on it.

C.q: When the alpha products are finished, Tom Achebe tells Hannah Okoro that the work package is complete and hands it back, and project support is told so it can update the registers. Is this an appropriate application of the 'notify work package completion' activity, and why?
options: Yes, because completion goes back to the PM, who issued the package
Yes, because the senior supplier must be told each package is done
No, because completion should be reported to the board directly
No, because the products must first pass the accessibility audit
C.why: Just as the work package was accepted from the PM, its completion must be notified back to the PM; project support is informed (17.4.4, table 17.2).

whyNot.1: The senior supplier is not informed of work package completion in the RACI.
whyNot.2: The board is not involved in MP; completion goes to the PM, who receives it in controlling a stage.
whyNot.3: The independent audit is a go-live condition for the service, not a step in notifying completion of an alpha work package.

C.q: Tom Achebe accepts the alpha work package without checking whether the council tax integration can be built in ten weeks, even though the council's ICT team is stretched across three other projects. Halfway through, it is clear the integration cannot be delivered on time. Was the 'accept a work package' activity applied appropriately, and why?
options: Yes, because the PM authorized the package in controlling a stage
Yes, because the time tolerance in the package will absorb a delay
No, because a team plan is needed before a package can be accepted
No, because accepting includes agreeing that the work is achievable
C.why: Accept a work package includes agreeing whether the requirements are reasonable and can be achieved before the team manager agrees to deliver (17.4.1).

whyNot.0: The PM's authorization does not replace the team manager's check that the work can be achieved.
whyNot.1: Tolerance allows limited deviation; it does not make an unachievable work package acceptable.
whyNot.2: A team plan is optional; the failing was not agreeing that the work was achievable.

reteach.title: Receive, build, report, hand back
reteach.question: Think of the team manager as a contractor receiving a job sheet. What happens when the job is taken on, while it is worked, and when it is handed back?

blocks.body: Taking on the job is accept a work package: agree what, how to report, constraints and whether it is achievable. Working the job is execute a work package: build to the sheet, tell the PM about new issues, risks and lessons, record quality checks. Showing progress is evaluate a work package. Handing the job back is notify work package completion.

blocks.text: Execute RACI: PM accountable, project assurance consulted, business layer and executive not involved. Notify completion: project support informed.

explain.body: Before work is allocated, the PM and team manager agree what is to be delivered, reporting requirements, constraints, procedures and whether the work is reasonable and achievable, including its tolerances. The team manager then agrees to deliver it and may produce a team plan.

test.q: Hannah Okoro and Tom Achebe agree a scope tolerance that lets the business-permit journey be left out of the alpha if time runs short, and Tom then agrees to deliver the work package. Which activity is being applied?
options: Execute a work package
Accept a work package
Evaluate a work package
Notify work package completion
test.why: Agreeing the work package's requirements, including its tolerances, before the team manager agrees to deliver it is accept a work package (17.4.1).

whyNot.0: Execute is the building of the products once the work package has been accepted.
whyNot.2: Evaluate reports results back to the PM; nothing has been built yet.
whyNot.3: Notifying completion happens at the end, when the products are finished.

explain.body: The team manager manages the building of the products to the work package requirements, notifies the PM of any new issues, risks or lessons and takes any action the PM requires, notifies completed quality activities and updates the quality register, and reports status through checkpoint reports.

test.q: During the alpha, Tom Achebe's team learns that the national vehicle records interface the service relies on may change next year. This is a new risk to the project. What should Tom do?
options: Raise an exception report to the project board
Ask Graham Pell, the executive, how to respond
Notify Hannah Okoro and act as she requires
Record it in the risk management approach
test.why: In execute a work package the team manager notifies the PM of any new issues, risks or lessons and takes any action the PM requires (17.4.2).

whyNot.0: Exception reports are raised by the PM to the board when stage tolerance is forecast to be exceeded; the team manager reports to the PM.
whyNot.1: The executive is not involved in MP; the team manager's route is to the PM.
whyNot.3: The risk management approach sets procedures; specific risks are recorded in the risk register, via the PM.

explain.body: Evaluate a work package reports results back to the PM so progress is clearly visible to the project management team. Notify work package completion returns the finished work package to the PM, just as it was accepted from the PM; the PM then receives it in controlling a stage.

test.q: Tom Achebe notifies Hannah Okoro that every product in the alpha work package is finished. Which 'controlling a stage' activity does Hannah use to deal with this notification?
options: Receive completed work package
Evaluate work package status
Evaluate stage status
Authorize a work package
test.why: Notify work package completion in MP is matched by receive completed work package in CS, where the PM checks approvals and updates the product register (16.4.3, 17.4.4).

whyNot.1: Evaluate work package status is used while the work is under way, using checkpoint reports.
whyNot.2: Evaluate stage status compares the whole stage with its plan; it is not the hand-back point for one work package.
whyNot.3: Authorize a work package starts work; this notification closes it.

explain.body: Execute a work package: the PM is accountable, the team manager responsible for the work and its checkpoint reports, project assurance consulted; the business layer and the executive are not involved. Notify work package completion: project support is informed; the business layer, senior user and senior supplier are not.

explain.h: Who is in, who is out
head: Activity
Takes part
No part
rows: Business layer, senior user, senior supplier

test.q: Graham Pell, executive for Permits Online, asks which roles take part when Kestrel Lane's team builds the products under its work package. Which roles have no part in the 'execute a work package' activity?
options: Project assurance and the executive
The project manager and the business layer
Project assurance and the business layer
The business layer and the executive
test.why: The business layer and the executive are not involved in execute a work package; the PM is accountable and project assurance consulted (17.6, table 17.2).

whyNot.0: Project assurance is consulted in execute a work package, so it does take part.
whyNot.1: The project manager is accountable for execute a work package.
whyNot.2: Project assurance is consulted; only the business layer of this pair has no part.
